title: On the instability of some upward propagating, exact, nonlinear mountain waves: the unstable set of stratified layers (Theorem 13)
author: Christian Puntini
work: On the instability of some upward propagating, exact, nonlinear mountain waves
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's real-analyticity and structure theorem for the discriminant of stratified layers, printed as Theorem 13 (source0.tex lines 1040-1050) and delivered with the paper's own complete 185-line proof (lines 1052-1236). The statement gives three things at once: the real-analyticity of Delta on the parameter domain; the openness of the unstable set with a whole segment of instability at vanishing stratification, hence a small-stratification instability threshold nu_*(e) for every e > 1/3; and the exact local description of the neutral curve near the degenerate point (1/3,0), including the second-order expansion e_c(nu^2) = 1/3 - (4/9) nu^2 + O(nu^4). The proof is a source-local analysis that has to be assembled rather than quoted: analyticity from the parameter dependence of the fundamental matrix of a linear ODE system and its trace at one period; the implicit function theorem applied to Delta + 2 = 0 at the degenerate point, with the two partial derivatives computed from the explicit hyperbolic-cosine series and its parameter dependence; a perturbation expansion in the stratification to obtain the second-order coefficient of the neutral curve; and the boundary values at vanishing steepness, where the discriminant collapses to 2 cos(2 pi nu) or 2 cosh(2 pi |nu|) and the closure of the unstable set meets the axis only at the resonant values. No qualifying examination poses a three-part stability diagram for a compressible stratified shear layer together with the local shape of its neutral curve and the resonant structure on the degenerate axis; the unit is H2.
